session_title: Enterprise Intrusion & Cyber Kill Chain Simulation

alerts.title: Automated Credential Brute-Force Attack
alerts.description: Detected 7 failed authentication attempts from IP 198.51.100.77 targeting user(s) root, admin, test, ubuntu, webuser. [!] CRITICAL: Followed by a successful login! Account likely compromised.
evidence_samples: Oct 29 02:12:10 auth-server sshd[14012]: Failed password for invalid user root from 198.51.100.77 port 48912 ssh2
Oct 29 02:12:12 auth-server sshd[14015]: Failed password for invalid user admin from 198.51.100.77 port 48914 ssh2
Oct 29 02:12:14 auth-server sshd[14018]: Failed password for invalid user ubuntu from 198.51.100.77 port 48916 ssh2

playbook.detection_summary: Automated credential brute-force attack detected from source 198.51.100.77 targeting account 'root'.
containment_actions: Immediately block incoming connections from IP 198.51.100.77 at network border firewall.
Temporarily lock or enforce password reset for targeted account 'root'.
Verify fail2ban or SSH rate-limiting policies are operating.
playbook.containment_command: sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 198.51.100.77 -j DROP  # (Windows: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="TraceGuard_Block_198.51.100.77" dir=in action=block remoteip=198.51.100.77)
eradication_steps: Inspect auth.log for any successful logins from this IP during the same timeframe.
Revoke any active SSH sessions or OAuth tokens associated with the account.
Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) on all remote access endpoints.
recovery_steps: Restore account access after user identity verification.
Verify host integrity and review system process lists for unauthorized background daemons.
Monitor auth logs for secondary attack waves.
playbook.compliance_impact: PCI-DSS 8.1.6 (Account lockout after repeated attempts) & 10.2 (Audit log monitoring).

alerts.title: Directory Traversal / Arbitrary File Read
alerts.description: Detected 2 directory traversal probes attempt to read sensitive system files (e.g. /etc/passwd).

playbook.detection_summary: Web application exploit attempt (SQL Injection / Directory Traversal) originating from 198.51.100.88.
containment_actions: Blacklist 198.51.100.88 at the Web Application Firewall (WAF) or reverse proxy layer.
Isolate affected web application instances from sensitive internal backend database segments.
Capture live packet traces and preserve raw HTTP access logs for digital forensics.
playbook.containment_command: sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 198.51.100.88 -j DROP  # (Windows: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="TraceGuard_Block_198.51.100.88" dir=in action=block remoteip=198.51.100.88)
eradication_steps: Audit web server code and sanitize input parameters (apply prepared statements / parameterized queries).
Verify web directory permissions to ensure read-only status for non-upload paths.
Scan filesystem for newly dropped webshells or modified scripts.
recovery_steps: Deploy patched application code to production.
Conduct regression testing and automated vulnerability scan via VigilScan.
Re-enable public web routing through WAF.
playbook.compliance_impact: GDPR Article 33 (Assess potential personal data breach within 72 hours) & PCI-DSS 6.5 (Prevent common web vulnerabilities).

alerts.title: Suspicious Administrative Privilege Escalation
alerts.description: User 'webuser' executed high-risk command via sudo: '/bin/bash'.
evidence_samples: Oct 29 02:18:05 auth-server sudo: webuser : TTY=pts/1 ; PWD=/home/webuser ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/bash

playbook.detection_summary: Unauthorized privilege escalation or off-hours sudo execution detected by user 'webuser'.
containment_actions: Suspend user account 'webuser' immediately and terminate active shell sessions (`pkill -u webuser`).
Freeze endpoint state or snapshot virtual machine to preserve volatile memory evidence.
playbook.containment_command: sudo usermod -L webuser ; sudo pkill -u webuser
eradication_steps: Audit /etc/sudoers file for unauthorized NOPASSWD entries or modified permissions.
Inspect user bash history (.bash_history) and recently modified files in /tmp and /var/tmp.
Check cron jobs (`/etc/cron*`) and systemd services for persistence mechanisms.
recovery_steps: Re-image compromised host if root compromise is confirmed.
Re-issue all SSH keys and administrative credentials.
Perform formal Post-Incident Review (Lessons Learned) within 5 business days.
playbook.compliance_impact: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312 (Audit Controls) & GDPR Article 32 (Security of processing).

alerts.title: Network Service Discovery / Port Reconnaissance
alerts.description: Host 203.0.113.55 performed horizontal/vertical port sweep across 6 destination ports (21, 22, 80, 443, 3306, 8080).
evidence_samples: Oct 29 02:10:01 edge-gateway kernel: [UFW BLOCK] IN=eth0 OUT= SRC=203.0.113.55 DST=10.0.0.5 PROTO=TCP DPT=21
Oct 29 02:10:02 edge-gateway kernel: [UFW BLOCK] IN=eth0 OUT= SRC=203.0.113.55 DST=10.0.0.5 PROTO=TCP DPT=22
Oct 29 02:10:03 edge-gateway kernel: [UFW BLOCK] IN=eth0 OUT= SRC=203.0.113.55 DST=10.0.0.5 PROTO=TCP DPT=80

playbook.detection_summary: Reconnaissance port scanning activity detected from IP 203.0.113.55.
containment_actions: Drop all traffic from reconnaissance host 203.0.113.55.
Verify external firewall rules drop unsolicited SYN probes without responding with RST packets.
playbook.containment_command: sudo iptables -A INPUT -s 203.0.113.55 -j DROP  # (Windows: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="TraceGuard_Block_203.0.113.55" dir=in action=block remoteip=203.0.113.55)
eradication_steps: Audit perimeter network to verify no unneeded management ports are exposed.
Check IDS/IPS signature databases to ensure automated blacklisting is synchronized.
recovery_steps: Continue passive telemetry monitoring for correlation with subsequent exploit attempts.
Log scanning source IP into threat intelligence sharing feed.
playbook.compliance_impact: SOC 2 & ISO 27001 Perimeter Defense & Attack Surface Management controls.
